ending1.title: The Steward Dismissed
ending1.subtitle: The chancery does not judge you. The chancery handles dates
ending1.text:
The letter came on the first of November. The chancery seal.

The temporary residence and labour guarantee numbered VS-18-0947 expired on the thirtieth of October. No renewal was submitted by the guarantor. Under Chapter Fourteen of the Basic Law, the holder is required to depart the territory of the Kingdom of Marigni within seven days of expiry.

Below that, in small type: this letter does not constitute an assessment of the holder’s performance of service.

You read the letter twice. The second time you read the small type.

Packing took half a morning.

You do not have much. You came with one case and you leave with one case. The general ledger for the month stays on the desk. It is not yours.

The pale rectangle on the right-hand side of the desk is still there. You never did work out what used to stand on it.

Martha made up a parcel of food for you. Handing it over she said “for the road”, and then turned back into the kitchen, walking faster than she usually walks.

Elena is not there. All morning she is not where she ought to be.

Gregor brought the cart round.

Nobody told him to take you. He went and did it himself.

It is forty minutes from the estate to Valehold North. You go by the road you came in on, except that this time there is nothing on the maples. The leaves all came down in last week’s frost, and the two rows of branches are bare, and you can see the sky.

Thirty-one days ago this road was burning.

He does not say one word.

At the platform he lifts the case down and sets it on the steps. The same movement as thirty-one days ago, in the other direction.

variants.stable_repaired:
“The roof will not leak this year,” he says.

Then he leads the horse away.
variants.plain:
“Mind the road.”

Then he leads the horse away.
variants.henk:
The west store room was locked while you were packing.

You take nothing out of it. None of it was yours, and none of it ever was.

You left a note for the next steward, setting it out plainly: that the goods came from Millridge, when they came, how much of it there was, and that none of it is in the books.

You looked at it a long time after you had written it, and then you tore it up.

The next one will find it out.

Or will not.
variants.early:
The Baron’s man came in the morning.

Not a letter from the chancery. The chancery handles dates, and this did not wait for a date.

What he brought was the Baron’s own hand, half a sheet, written quickly.

“Payment stops today. Hand over within three days.”

Maplegate settled not one account this month. The day-labourers’ wages, the smith’s bill, the flour cart that comes every week — all of them entered in your ledger, all of them blank.

A thing like that travels faster than other things. By the time the note arrived, three houses in Valehold had already stopped giving Maplegate credit.

The tenants made no trouble. They simply stopped coming. In those last days there were fewer of them in the fields each day, and standing on the bank in the morning what you saw was wheat with nobody cutting it.

The handover took three days. Elena laid out every document for the man who came, not one of them missing, done more carefully than she did it while you were here.

He asked her where the month’s record of expenditure was.

She said there had been no expenditure.

On the morning you left, Martha cooked as she always does, half an hour earlier than usual. She put a parcel on the table and went back into the kitchen without speaking.

Gregor brought the cart round.

Nobody told him to take you. He went and did it himself.

It is forty minutes from the estate to Valehold North. The wheat is still in the fields, and the two rows of maples have not dropped their leaves. This autumn is only half over.

He does not say one word.

At the platform he lifts the case down and sets it on the steps.

ending2.title: The Competent Outsider
ending2.subtitle: You stayed, and what told you so was a letter
ending2.text: The letter came on the thirty-first of October. This time it is the Baron’s own hand.

variants.lord_warm:
The renewal has been signed and is enclosed. Submit it to the chancery within seven days.

I have seen the harvest figures. For one month, properly handled.

von Alder
variants.lord_plain:
The renewal has been signed and is enclosed. Submit it to the chancery within seven days.

Have a fair copy of this quarter’s general ledger and of the tenant roll sent in with the renewal.

von Alder
variants.tail:
That is all of it.

You stayed.

You put the letter on the desk with the renewal underneath it. There is a blank on it, in the same place as on the guarantee thirty days ago, waiting for your name.

You signed.

You sit in the office and hear the kitchen below. Today is no different from yesterday, and tomorrow will be no different from today.

You stayed, and what told you so was a letter.
variants.henk:
On the day the renewal came through you went out to the west store room.

It is all still there. You counted it over: grain, timber, that cloth sack. The same as the night it was loaded.

You locked the door.

You stayed. Part of the reason for that is in this room, and the key to this room now hangs at your belt.

ending3.title: One of the Valley
ending3.subtitle: Nobody announced anything. Nobody read out any terms
ending3.text: The letter came on the thirty-first of October. This time it is the Baron’s own hand.

variants.letter:
The renewal has been signed and is enclosed. Submit it to the chancery within seven days.

I have seen the harvest figures. For one month, properly handled.

von Alder
variants.marguerite_line: Appended: the Baroness at Thornwall wrote and mentioned you. She very seldom mentions anybody.
variants.feast:
The Kindling falls in the first week of November.

For the three days before it nobody on the estate does any proper work. Martha fills the kitchen; the women from the tenant households all come, and from morning to night they are pickling and rendering and putting things down into jars. Elena washes every window in the main house, the high ones included, which are washed once a year. Gregor hangs a bundle of dry branches over the stable door and does not explain what it is for; you learn later that it is the custom here.

Master Lorenz brings the wood for the new fire. Branches down off that old oak at the hunting ground, divided between the three estates.

The fire in the forge-chapel has to be put out once on the night before, and then lit again with the new wood. It is the one time in the year the hearth is allowed to go cold.

You watch him do it. He presses out the last of the coals, tests the heat of the hearth with the back of his hand, and starts laying the new wood.

“This one night every year,” he says. “It must not be cold for long.”

You stand beside him and keep the draught off while he lights it.

At midday on the day itself the estate’s long table is set out in the courtyard.

Twenty-odd tenant households come. Old Wendt brings his grandson, and the boy keeps looking over towards the stable. Martha’s dishes come out from midday until dark, and not one of them is anything you ever saw in Forgehold.

You are seated in the middle of the table. Not at the head; the head is empty. That is the Baron’s place, and he does not arrive until tomorrow.

Halfway through the meal you find that something has appeared in front of you.
variants.unadmitted:
A small dish of something pickled, which last month, in the kitchen, you happened to say you liked.

Martha is not looking at you. She is at the other end of the table filling glasses, and her laugh carries over everybody else’s talking.

You finished the dish.

After dark people start to go. The tenant households leave one at a time, and they take their leave of you on the way out, and it is not the way people take leave of a steward. Old Wendt’s grandson runs over to ask whether he can come and help in the stable next spring, and his grandfather pulls him away.

Once the table is cleared the courtyard is empty.

You stand in the yard and look at the light over at the forge-chapel.

You have not worked out what happened today. You only stand there, and the day feels long, and you do not want it to end.
variants.admitted:
A small dish of something pickled, which last month, in the kitchen, you happened to say you liked.

Martha is not looking at you. She is at the other end of the table filling glasses, and her laugh carries over everybody else’s talking.

You think of the twenty-seventh of October, on that street in Valehold, and the one thing you said to two men who do not belong here either.

I want a standing of my own.

You did not know at the time exactly what that sentence meant. You meant the card with the maple-leaf pattern on it. You meant eight years. You meant a recommendation out of a local jurisdiction; Timothy read the terms out very clearly.

And now there is a dish of pickles in front of you.

Nobody announced anything. Nobody read out any terms. Martha simply remembered one thing you said last month, and today she put it in front of you.

You finished the dish.

After dark people start to go. The tenant households leave one at a time, and they take their leave of you on the way out, and it is not the way people take leave of a steward. Old Wendt’s grandson runs over to ask whether he can come and help in the stable next spring, and his grandfather pulls him away.

Once the table is cleared the courtyard is empty.

You stood in the yard a long time.

Eight years. You work it out: seven years and eleven months left.

You do not know whether you can last that long. You do not know whether you will be at this table this time next year.

But today somebody put a dish of pickles by for you, and that needs no document to prove it.
variants.henk:
After the table broke up, going back to the office, you passed the west store room.

It is all still in there. Grain, timber, and that cloth sack heavier than you expected.

You did not go in.

This time next year, or sooner, somebody will come over from Millridge about some very small thing.

ending4a.title: A Body Not Given to the Fire
ending4a.subtitle: A man spent seven weeks twelve kilometres from home
ending4a.text:
You gave Thierry what you had.

That was somewhere in the twenties of October. A cloth bundle with a few dried stems in it. A sheet of paper recording which way a horse’s shoe had worn when it came back, and how high the mud went on its legs. And a few lines you had copied out yourself.

You told him you could not work out where it was.

“I shall have to walk all three,” he said. “One a day.”

He walked for three days.

On the second of November he sent word that it had been found.

Not the easternmost one with the stone bottom, and not the shaded one in the middle. The highest of them. The hollow he had been into once, in summer.

From there to Maplegate is under twelve kilometres in a straight line.

A man spent seven weeks twelve kilometres from home.

You went that afternoon.

Thierry was waiting at the edge of the hollow with two men from the forestry district. He did not let you go all the way up.

“You do not need to,” he said. “I have looked.”

He described what he had seen. The ruin of a stone wall, half a roof, enough to keep the wind off. Signs of a fire having been made, more than once. A water hollow weighted down with a stone, rigged by hand.

There was a wound on one leg, on the outside of the calf. Not deep, but it had gone a long time.

“Middle of October, about,” Thierry said. “That wet spell.”

You think of those days in the middle of October. You were reaping. The weather was bad. You had worked out how much it was going to cost you.

He had very little with him.

A coat, a knife, a tin cup. And a wooden box.

Handing you the box, Thierry said he had not opened it.

You did not open it there either. You put it in an inside pocket, carried it all the way back to the estate, and set it on the office desk.

It came to rest exactly on the pale rectangle.

All four edges square.

You opened it.

Two things inside.

A certificate from the Valehold Lyceum of Stewardship. Land management. Dated twelve years ago.

A photograph. Four people standing in front of the main door of Maplegate — the same few steps you stood on thirty days ago with your case in your hand. An old gentleman on the left. On the right a middle-aged man in a steward’s clothes. Between them two young ones, one in his twenties and one about ten.

On the back of the photograph is a single line in pencil, in the child’s hand, pressed hard into the paper:

He took nothing with him when he went. He took this.

variants.rites_open:
Lorenz conducted the rite, set for the third day after the Kindling.

It was the first time in forty years he had done it for somebody who had not died on an estate. He said that by the practice there is no difference: a return to the fire is a return to the fire, and where a man stopped does not affect the hearth.

More people came than you expected. People from the three estates, tenants, several out from Valehold. Timothy came as well, in uniform, standing in the last row. He does not know Hartmann’s family. He only dealt with him for three years.

Martha stood at the very front the whole way through. She did not cry. Her face was held very tight.
variants.elena_present: She came, and stood at the outside of the crowd, as far from the hearth as it was possible to stand. She never once moved forward.
variants.rites_close:
The hearth was opened.

A wave of heat came out and struck your face, and that temperature is not the temperature of a fireplace. It is something else. In that instant you understood something nobody had explained to you in thirty days: why this country built everything it has on fire.

You stood in the crowd and waited with them.
variants.ludwig:
He arrived on the third of November, two days earlier than other years.

He did not have himself announced. You were in the office, heard movement below, and by the time you came down he was standing in the hall with his coat still on.

“Where is it.”

You brought the box down and gave it to him.

He opened it and looked once. Only once. He did not take the photograph out. He knew what was in there.

He closed the box, set it on the narrow table in the hall, put both hands flat on the lid and stood there a while.

“Ninety-six,” he said.

He did not explain what happened that year.

After a while he asked a few specific questions. Who found him. Whereabouts. Whether the rite had been held. Who came to it. You answered each one.

He heard all of it out.

And then he said something you were not prepared for.

“He did not talk much as a boy,” he said. “I am ten years older. He was running about here with his father while I was at school in Forgehold and came home twice a year. He was always sitting on those steps by the door.”

He glanced at the door. It stood open, and the steps were in view.

“I never asked him what he wanted to do.”

He took his hands off the box.

“I thought that was not mine to ask.”
variants.festival_mirror:
The Kindling falls three days after the return to the fire.

The estate’s long table is set out in the courtyard as always. Twenty-odd tenant households come, the same number as other years; nobody stays away because of what happened a few days ago. The custom here runs like this: what has to be done is done, one thing at a time, and when it is done you keep the feast.

You sit in the middle of the table. The head is empty; the Baron leaves tomorrow.

Halfway through the meal a dish appears in front of you. Pickled. The thing you happened to say in the kitchen last month that you liked.

Martha is at the other end of the table filling glasses, and does not look at you.

There is one more place laid at the foot of the table, with nobody in it.

You ask Martha who it is for.

“It is laid every year,” she says. “It is laid this year too.”

Then she turns away to fetch the wine.
variants.henk:
On the day of the return to the fire you stood in the crowd.

People came from all three estates. Two came from Millridge — not Henk himself; he sent his steward.

After the rite the Millridge steward came over and said a few civil things. That the Baron sent his regards. That it had been a hard autumn. That neighbours ought to help one another.

While he was speaking you were thinking about what is in the west store room.

The man lying in that fire is lying there because he refused Henk.

And part of the reason you are standing here, able to hand the estate over, is that you did not.

You thanked the steward.

ending4b.title: 一个被找回来的人
ending4b.subtitle: 等着的东西来了，你也已经不是当初等它的那个人了
ending4b.text:
你把手上的东西摊在蒂埃里面前的时候，他没有花很长时间。

“最高那一处。”他说，“有水，背阴，长这种草。另外两个不长。”

他当天就带了两个人上去。

第二天傍晚他们把人抬回来了。

他还活着。

小腿外侧有一处伤，不深，但发过炎，肿到膝盖。他已经发热了好几天，蒂埃里说再晚三四天就不好说了。

他瘦得脱了形。抬进来的时候他睁着眼，看了看门厅的天花板，然后看向抬他的人，然后又看回天花板。

他没有认出这是哪儿。

玛莎在门厅站着，两只手抓着围裙。她一句话也没说，这是全故事里她唯一一次说不出话。

格雷格去河谷城请医生，来回花了三个钟头，比平时快了一半。

他在床上躺了很久。

前十天他大部分时间在睡。埃莱娜照顾他。

这件事没有人安排，也没有人商量。第一天晚上她就搬了张椅子进那间屋，从那以后每天换药、擦身、喂东西、半夜起来看他有没有发热，都是她。

玛莎默认了。玛莎什么都没说。

有一天你路过那间屋，门开着一条缝。她正在把一块湿布从他额头上拿下来，换一块新的。她的动作很轻，很熟练，那是她做了十天之后的熟练。

她抬头看见你了。

她没有像以前那样低下头去。她朝你点了一下头，然后继续手上的事。

那个木匣在他身上。

抬他回来的时候从外套内侧掉出来的，蒂埃里捡起来放在了床头。

七个星期，他一直带着。

variants.awake:
他能坐起来说话，是十一月中旬的事。

那时候你已经在这座庄园里待了六个星期，你的续签下来了，第二期是九十天。

你去看他。他坐在床上，背后垫着枕头，膝上放着一块板子，埃莱娜找来的，让他可以看东西。

板子上什么也没有。

“您就是新来的管事。”他说。

声音很轻，但很清楚。他说话的方式和你想象的一样，精确，一句是一句。

你说是。

“庄园的事我问过了。”他说。

你愣了一下。

“玛莎在这儿坐了两回。格雷格来过一次，站在门口，说了三句话。”他说，“埃莱娜每天都在。”

他把膝上那块板子挪了挪。

“秋收的数字、税缴了多少、佃户那五户修了几家、林地边界的事查到哪儿，我都知道了。”

“所以我不问您这些。”

他停了一下。

“而且这些事怎么办的，已经把您是什么样的人说清楚了。”

他说这句话的时候语气很平，那不是称赞，是一个做过八年管家的人在陈述一件他有能力判断的事。

房间里安静了一会儿。窗外是枫径大道的方向，树已经空了。

然后他问了。

“那我问别的。”

“您为什么要留下来？”
variants.admitted:
你说了那句话。

十月二十七日在河谷城那条街上，你对两个不属于这里的人说过它。那两个人一个是被派来的，一个是自己挣来位置的。

但这一次你说得比那一次长。

因为那天在街上你说的是那张卡片，带枫叶纹样的那张，八年，一份来自本地司法辖区的推荐。你当时以为自己想要的是那个。

现在你说的是别的东西。你说了几件很具体的事。它们加起来不成一个理由，但你说完之后自己知道那就是理由。
variants.unadmitted:
你没有说好。

你说的不是合同，也不是期限，这些话你说不出口了，它们在两个月前是真的，现在不是了。

你说的是一些具体的事。厨房里那个位置。马厩早上的味道。霜降那天田里没有人说话的样子。有一次你在炉堂坐了一下午，什么也没想。

你说得很乱。你说完之后觉得自己什么都没有回答。

他没有追问。
variants.after:
他听完了，看着窗外。

“这儿的人有句话。”他说，“有些东西靠的是等待。”

“这话是真的。我信了三十年。”

他把手放在膝上那块空板子上。

“但他们不说后半句。”

“等着的东西来了，你也已经不是当初等它的那个人了。”

房间里很静。楼下有人在走动，大概是埃莱娜。

“凯斯勒跟您说过年限吗。”他忽然问。

你说过。八年，加一份本地司法辖区的推荐。

“他说得没错。条款是那样。”

他停了一会儿。

“但八年不只是八年。八年是一个人变一遍的时间。”

“您现在决定的事，是八年之后那个人来兑现的。而那个人不是您。”

他说这句话的时候没有任何劝阻的意思。他不是在说“所以别留下”。

他是在说一件他确认过的事。
variants.continued:
过了一会儿他换了话头。

“我从这儿出去过两次。”他说，“学苑四年，在河谷城。毕业那年去了铸都，待了十一个月。”

“两次都回来了。”

他看向窗户。

“那趟车我坐过。三条隧道，两个山口，出最长那条的时候光会一下子涌进来。”

他顿了一下。

“但我坐的两次都是回来。我不知道不再回来的路，是什么样？”

他转过头。

“您走过那条路。”

你跟他说了你走过那条路。

你没有说南坡的颜色，也没有说树冠从灰绿变成金色。那些他知道，他在这片林子里活了三十年。

你说的是别的。

你说你上车之前在站台上回过一次头。铸者之河对岸的北岸上城区在晨雾里只露出轮廓，冠焰宫的塔尖、圣堂的穹顶、君王之跃石桥连成一条淡灰色的天际线。

你说你当时想的是：我没来得及去那边看过。

然后你想的是：也许以后也不会。

你说你就是在想到第二句的时候，车门关上了。

他听完之后很久没有说话。

“我在铸都住了十一个月。”他说，“我一次也没有过河到北岸去。”

“十一个月。”

他看着自己的手。

“我一直想着回来以后有很多事要做。”

然后他问了第二个问题。

然后是第三个。
variants.ludwig:
他是十一月三日到的，比往年早了两天。

他直接上了二楼那间屋。

门关着，关了很久。你在楼下的办公室，什么也没有听见，那间屋的门很厚，而且他们两个人说话的声音本来都不大。

他下来的时候你正好在门厅。

他站在楼梯下面，一只手还搭在扶手上，没有立刻往前走。

“他问我铸都是什么样。”他说。

他没有说自己是怎么回答的。

过了一会儿他往门口走。走到门口他停下来，看着外面那几级台阶。

“他小时候总在这儿坐着。”他说，“我一年回来两回，每回他都在。”

“我没有问过他想做什么。”

他推开门走出去，站在台阶上，背对着你。

外面的枫树全空了。

“现在还来得及。”
variants.henk:
那天晚上你在办公室对账。西边储藏间里那些东西的来处，账上没有记。

你在纸上写了一行，又划掉了。

楼上那间屋的灯还亮着，埃莱娜在。

那个人躺在那张床上，是因为他拒绝了亨克，然后一个人扛了八年。

而你留在这座庄园里，有一部分原因是你没有拒绝。

你把那一页翻过去了。
variants.festival_mirror:
圣火节那天中午，庄园的长桌摆在庭院里。

他还上不了桌。埃莱娜端了一份上楼。

你坐在桌子中间。主位空着，男爵在楼上，他说他一会儿下来，后来没有下来。

吃到一半你面前多了一碟腌的东西，是你上个月随口说过喜欢的。玛莎在桌子另一头给人添酒，没有看你。

天黑之后人散了。你上楼的时候路过那间屋，门开着一条缝。

桌上有两个盘子。

一个是他的，吃了大半。

另一个在床边的凳子上，也吃了大半。

epilogue.title: 尾声 · 路德维希的三天
epilogue.text:
他每年圣火节回来，住三天。

他不进城。三天里他不去河谷城，不见任何邻庄的人，亨克每年都派人来递话，每年都被回掉。

他做的事不多。

variants.ending3: 他在长桌的主位上坐了那顿饭。他吃得很少，但他坐到了最后。
variants.ending4a: 他查账，但只翻了几页就合上了。三天里他去了两次门厅那张窄桌，木匣放在那儿。
variants.ending4b: 他上楼三次。第三次待了一个多小时。
variants.close:
第三天下午他走。

马车在庄园门口等着。他上车之前会做一件每年都做的事，他会在枫径大道的入口站一会儿，看那两排树。

十一月初，树已经空了。

格雷格说他年年都站。

“站多久？”

“不长。”格雷格说，“一分钟，两分钟。”

他上了车。马车沿着那条空掉的隧道往南走，走到看不见。

然后庄园安静下来。

冬天就要来了。
